flows.name: /orders - open the order list
flows.description: The read path. The interesting part is that nobody calls a load method: the resource reloads itself because the tenant signal it depends on changed.

steps.note: guard runs before the bundle is fetched
lazy chunk for @acme/orders
page reads state.orders()
rxResource triggers on the tenant signal
adds the bearer token to the request
GET /api/orders
customer names for the table column
filtered rows go down into the table
rendered by the generic table

flows.name: cancel an order
flows.description: A write path with an optimistic update: the row flips first, the request follows, and only an error rolls it back and reloads.

steps.note: table reports the click upwards
page forwards it to the state
state flips the row, then calls the api
adds the bearer token to the request
POST /api/orders/{id}/cancel
table re-renders from the changed signal

findings.title: OrderState reaches into the customers feature
findings.evidence: OrderState -> CustomerState, the only edge between the two feature libraries
findings.detail: Two feature libraries know each other, so neither can ship without the other. The dependency exists for one thing only: resolving customer names.
findings.suggestion: Let the order api return the name, or move the lookup into a shared library both may depend on.

findings.title: CustomerState loads the full customer list
findings.evidence: CustomerApi.loadAll(): GET /api/customers, no paging parameter in the signature
findings.detail: Fine while the list is short. The picker holds every customer in memory and the first slow render happens without any code change.
findings.suggestion: Paging or a search endpoint, before the number decides it for you.

findings.title: CustomerPickerPage has no organism between page and state
findings.evidence: CustomerPickerPage -> CustomerState directly, while OrderListPage goes through OrderTable
findings.detail: The two pages are built differently. Nothing is broken, it just means the picker's markup has nowhere to go when it grows.
findings.suggestion: Only worth doing when the page gets its second job.

findings.title: CustomerApi loads every customer once and nothing invalidates it
findings.evidence: httpResource in CustomerState, no signal it depends on, 3 journeys read it
findings.detail: The list is fetched on first read and kept for the rest of the session. A customer created in another tab is not in it, and no journey re-triggers the resource.
findings.suggestion: Give the resource a dependency it can react to, or reload it after the write journeys that change the list.
